title: Test a fractional Liouvillian square-function route for FI-2b
question: Can the finite-time local-Q2 shell be controlled by a fractional power of the bond Liouvillian, so that a local Dirichlet or Kubo--Mori estimate can replace the potentially cutoff-growing full commutator norm?
method: Use the exact B spectral blocks of the doubled bond and define the fractional seminorm |||ad_B|^theta X||_HS by energy-difference weights.
Apply the scalar interpolation min(2,|y|)<=2^(1-theta)|y|^theta for theta in {1/2,3/4,1} to obtain a finite-time shell bound.
Center the moved R-362 collision witness and remove B-commuting blocks with the R-364 spectral commutant before measuring the fractional shell.
Run a primary and non-importing independent reconstruction over every R-362 split orientation, sign, prefix, adjoint, beta and site, then compare all derived fields in an integrated verifier.
Compile Lean R366 for the theta=1/2 scalar envelope and the theta=1 reduction fixture; keep matrix exponentials and all limits in the executable lanes.
finding: R-366 closes the finite fractional interpolation pilot. Primary and independent lanes each pass 3082/3082 assertions over 768 contexts; integrated passes 46/46 and Lean R366 passes. The primary maximum phase-identity error is 6.178e-14, maximum fractional-envelope violation is 0, maximum fractional-bound violation is 6.176e-14, maximum state-trace violation is -2.756e-16, and the maximum primary-independent numeric difference is 6.661e-16. The largest finite-time-to-fractional-bound ratio is 0.999422.
decision_reason: The fractional phase envelope changes the decisive open analytic target from an unweighted first commutator to a fractional Liouvillian square function. At theta=1/2 this is compatible with local Dirichlet/Kubo--Mori forms and can exploit high-frequency interpolation without claiming a global energy estimate. The finite pilot verifies the algebra and identifies the next theorem, but it does not show that the fractional norm is uniform.

adversarial_review.check: The bound is derived from min(2,|y|), so it remains valid in both low- and high-frequency regimes; no Taylor estimate is used outside its range.
Zero energy differences contribute zero to the fractional seminorm and arbitrary matrices inside degenerate blocks are retained by spectral pinching.
The density-state trace step uses Hilbert--Schmidt Cauchy and does not assume [omega,B]=0.
The pilot samples V=2 and cutoffs 3,4 only; the fractional norm may still grow with cutoff, volume, source or prefix length.
The finite seminorm is unweighted; no Kubo--Mori weight, common core, or phase-conditioned form comparison has been proved.
Common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain outside the finite pilot.
The independent source reconstructs the finite system without importing the primary, and Lean R366 contains no sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe.

next_action: Stress theta=1/2 at larger cutoffs and graph volumes, then prove or refute a source- and volume-uniform local Kubo--Mori/Dirichlet comparison for the actual Q3 bond. If the fractional norm grows, record the exact growth rather than promote the finite interpolation.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite exact fractional spectral reduction and actual-Q3 diagnostic. No modular estimate, local collar, phase-weight theorem, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.
no_overclaim: R-366 supplies a finite interpolation inequality and a sharper analytic target only; it does not establish a regulator-uniform square function or any QFT limit.
